bullets.title: DELL: Blowout Quarter but Stock Down ~7% on Sustainability Concerns
bullets.body: Dell reported F3Q revenue of $54.94B (beat $49.32B est.), EPS $9.45 (beat $6.57), and raised FY27 revenue guide to $202B with AI server revenue ~$78B and backlog at $132.3B. FY28 EPS guided at $39.68 (~27% above consensus), and an additional $25B buyback was approved. Despite the beat, the stock is down ~7% premarket as the market debates CY28 DRAM pricing risk and broader AI capex sustainability; forward P/E has compressed to 8-9x from upper teens.

bullets.title: NVDA: $290M Class Action Settlement, Government Stake Speculation, Bearish Trend Signal
bullets.body: NVDA agreed to settle a 2018 class action for $290M over alleged crypto-mining GPU demand misrepresentation. Separately, Trump indicated the US could pursue an equity stake in NVDA, and a California AG investigation is ongoing. GPU pricing falling ~7% in Asia data centers; B300 lead times at 40 weeks. Hedgeye flagged a Bearish Trend signal since Oct 23rd; stock down ~6% premarket.

bullets.title: Broad Semiconductor Selloff: MU -9%, ARM -7%, AMD -7.3%, AVGO/ORCL at 52-Week Lows
bullets.body: The semiconductor sector is broadly lower with iShares SOXX ETF down 5.4% premarket. Notable declines: MU -9.0%, AMD -7.3%, ARM -7.0%, ALAB -7.1%, TSM -5.8%, INTC -5.1%, AVGO -24.9% YTD (at 52-week low), ORCL -50.1% YTD (52-week low), CLS -12.2%, FN -35.1%. Sell-side estimate cuts still seen as 2+ quarters away; frontier model revenue acceleration cited as the key sentiment catalyst.

bullets.title: GOOGL, NET, SNOW, PLTR: AI/Cloud Names Down 4-5% Premarket on Risk-Off
bullets.body: GOOGL down 5.4% and at 52-week lows (down 17% YTD); NET -4.5%, SNOW -4.5%, PLTR -4.5% in premarket. Citi maintained Buy on SNOW but cut PT to $470 from $490 on software multiple compression while flagging robust cRPO and AI contributing ~10pts to FY28 growth. CRWV down 48.4% YTD and IONQ down 56% YTD also at 52-week lows.

bullets.title: WDAY: F4Q Subscription Guide Disappoints; PT Cuts to $175-$200
bullets.body: Workday F3Q beat on revenue but F4Q subscription revenue guide of $2.600B misses consensus, implying deceleration from F3Q's +13% to ~+10% growth; FY28 target reiterates ~11%. Early renewals inflated cRPO, and five-year cohorts are renewing closer to three years. AI ARR at $750M+ growing 130% YoY but partially cannibalizing non-AI spend. Street cutting PTs to $175-$200 range.

bullets.title: META/AMZN: Muse Shopping Integration Discussions Resume After 2-Month Blockade
bullets.body: Meta and Amazon are in talks to restore Muse to Amazon's platform after a ~2-month blockade. Muse is simultaneously expanding to Instagram, Apple Messages, and Walmart Agent Gateway, and recently launched in UK, Japan, Singapore, Canada, Australia, and Mexico. Muse ranked 3rd in Citi's holiday shopping survey behind ChatGPT and retailer bots; Citi's survey shows 2026 holiday spend +12% YoY with K-shaped consumer trends.

bullets.title: SHOP: JPM Reiterates OW/$200 PT; BFCM >30% GMV Growth Is the Key Test
bullets.body: JPM highlights SHOP enterprise activity accelerating (~14 announcements in 3Q vs. 10 in 2Q) with enterprise estimated at ~5% of revenue in 2026 rising to ~7% in 2027. The $25M+ merchant cohort is the fastest-growing, with $100M+ cohort roughly doubling over two years. BFCM 2025 showed 27% YoY GMV growth; investors expect >30% in 2026, described as a high bar. SHOP also down 5.5% in Canadian trading on broad sector weakness.

bullets.title: GOOGL: Neon API Sets Day-1 Usage Record; Models Surpass OpenAI on OpenRouter Spend
bullets.body: Google's Neon model set a Day-1 usage record on paid APIs, with Antigravity tokens/day up 82% since Argon launched. Google models commanded >50% of OpenRouter spend vs. OpenAI for the first time since June 8th following Gemini 4 Neon and Carbon releases, signaling commercial adoption gains. Despite strong model momentum, GOOGL stock is down ~5% premarket and at 52-week lows.

bullets.title: AI Capex Financing Stress: JPM Forecasts $1.4T in 2027 Capex but Growth Decelerates After
bullets.body: JPM forecasts AI capex doubling to $1.4T in 2027 with 23 GW under construction and 97 GW committed, but growth decelerates materially in 2028+ as equity financing rises and debt markets hit capacity. Hedgeye flags HSBC sold $300M datacenter loans at 85 cents on the dollar and an ING $500M auction failed. Anthropic's Nexus Hubbard project delayed bond sale is backstopped by Google pending air permit approval before January 2027.

bullets.title: CRM: KeyBanc Flags F3Q27 Organic Bookings Test; Agentforce ROI Uncertainty Persists
bullets.body: KeyBanc notes CRM's F3Q27 guidance implies bookings growth slowing to ~6.0% cc from F2Q27's 7.5% rebound, putting organic demand in the spotlight. Agentforce adoption is improving but ROI/pricing uncertainty is limiting broad enterprise adoption, and it is not yet center of customer AI strategies. IT budgets continue to favor hardware, cybersecurity, and AI-native solutions over incumbent application software.

bullets.title: ADSK: Beat/Raise but PT Cut on Q4 Growth Slowdown; Stock Down ~5%
bullets.body: Autodesk raised FY revenue guidance to $8.360-8.375B with op margin of 39.2%-39.3% above consensus, but Q4 organic growth is slowing. Citi cut PT to $260 from $276 and is modestly more cautious on the FY28 growth algorithm. Stock is down ~5% in a weak tech tape despite the beat.

bullets.title: EXPE: Acquires Kiwi.com; Deal Expected to Close H1 2027
bullets.body: Expedia Group entered an agreement to acquire Kiwi.com, a Czech Republic-based online travel agency and travel technology company. Financial terms were not disclosed; transaction expected to close in H1 2027.

bullets.title: NFLX/DIS: Streaming Pricing Pressure as Consumers Trade Down
bullets.body: Citi flags NFLX and DIS facing pricing pressure as consumers shift to cheaper or free alternatives. Disney+ price has tripled since its 2019 launch versus ~50% growth for Netflix and 32% overall CPI inflation. The divergence is flagged as a potential consumer elasticity risk heading into 2027.

bullets.title: CLS: Down 12.2% on Broad Semiconductor Pressure; Now Down 47% YTD
bullets.body: Celestica is down 12.2% in Canadian trading and has fallen 47% YTD, now hitting 52-week lows alongside broader semiconductor and AI infrastructure names selling off on sustainability concerns. No specific fundamental catalyst cited beyond sector-wide pressure.

bullets.title: VRT, COHR, LITE, CIEN, ANET: Optical/Networking Down 4-7% in AI Infrastructure Selloff
bullets.body: Optical and networking equipment names are broadly lower premarket: VRT -6.7%, LITE -6.9%, CIEN -6.3%, COHR -6.2% as AI infrastructure sentiment deteriorates. ANET also lower. The selloff is driven by concerns over AI capex sustainability, data center demand deceleration, and GPU pricing declines.

bullets.title: Macro: Q3 GDP Revised to 4.3%, Core PCE at 3.26% YoY — Fed to Stay Hawkish
bullets.body: Q3 GDP was revised sharply higher to 4.3% from 3.4% on stronger personal consumption (4.2%) and capex (16.1%); domestic profit margins hit a record 17.4% in Q3. October core PCE came in at 0.293% MoM / 3.26% YoY with worsening inflation breadth (~50-52% of components running >3%). Consensus expects a 25bp Fed cut in December with hawkish guidance; meaningful equity weakness could cause the Fed to pause.

bullets.title: SPHR/MSG: JPM Hosting Investor Lunch Dec 3; Rates SPHR Overweight
bullets.body: JPM is hosting an investor lunch with MSG Entertainment SVP IR Ari Danes on December 3rd in NYC. JPM analyst David Karnovsky rates MSGK, MSGR, and SPHR ($4.5B market cap) all Overweight.

bullets.title: CEG, OKLO, SMR, TLN, ENPH, UEC: Goldman Energy Conference Jan 5-7
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs Energy, CleanTech & Utilities Conference is scheduled for January 5-7, 2027 in Miami, with CEG, ENPH, OKLO, SMR, TLN, and UEC among universe names participating. 1x1 meeting requests are being accepted for newly added companies.

bullets.title: CASY, MUSA: KeyBanc Reiterates OW on C-Store Strength from ATD's F2Q Beat
bullets.body: KeyBanc maintains Overweight on CASY ($780 PT, 33.1x 2028E EPS $23.60) and MUSA ($680 PT, 21.6x 2027E EPS $31.50) following Alimentation Couche-Tard's F2Q adjusted EPS of $0.84 vs. $0.80 consensus, with U.S. fuel margin at 48.1 CPG and U.S. same-store merchandise revenue +1.8% (sixth consecutive quarter of growth). ATD guided 15% EPS growth FY26-FY30 and net leverage improved to 1.72x, below the 2.0-2.5x target.

bullets.title: Growth vs. Non-Growth Rotation Accelerates: Ratio Down 18% Since Oct 7
bullets.body: The Growth/Non-Growth ratio fell another 4% today, extending an 18% decline since October 7, 2026. Non-Growth sectors (Basic Materials, Energy, Financials, Industrials) are outperforming Growth (Tech, Consumer Discretionary) as the market rotates toward cyclical/value. Multiple universe growth names are hitting 52-week lows: BKNG -25.9%, HOOD -46%, IONQ -56%, CRWV -48.4%.
